Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint against USAA Federal Savings Bank regarding its repeated refusal to properly process and resolve a valid debit card dispute, despite clear written documentation from the merchant confirming that I am owed a refund and that the refund must be handled through my bank by way of dispute. On XX/XX/XXXX, I prepaid {$420.00} for airport parking using my USAA American Express credit card. On XX/XX/XXXX, when exiting the airport parking garage, I was required to pay again at the exit in the amount of {$630.00}, and the only way to pay at the exit was with a XXXX card. Because of that system limitation, I used my USAA Visa debit card to pay the {$630.00} exit amount. After being charged this exit amount, I contacted the merchant, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, to address the overcharge and request the appropriate refund. The merchant responded to me by email and clearly stated that a {$140.00} overstay fee was incurred, but that I should dispute {$490.00} of the {$630.00} exit charge with my bank. The merchant explicitly wrote that they had validated the issue, that the most efficient way to refund me was through a credit card dispute, that they could not access my exit payment card information to refund me directly, and that if my bank submitted a dispute for exactly {$490.00}, they would honor it and the amount would not be placed back on my card. They also stated that if a different amount were disputed, it would be denied. This written statement is critical because it confirms three things : first, that I am owed {$490.00} back ; second, that the merchant could not process the refund directly ; and third, that the merchant specifically instructed me to recover the amount through my bank dispute process. Based on that written instruction from the merchant, I submitted a dispute with USAA on XX/XX/XXXX for the exact amount of {$490.00}. The same day, USAA sent me a letter requesting evidence to support the claim. I promptly submitted the ticket stub from the parking transaction and the merchants email through the USAA website portal. In other words, I provided the exact supporting documentation necessary to show that the merchant acknowledged the refund was owed and had directed me to pursue it through my bank. Despite that documentation, on XX/XX/XXXX, USAA sent me a notice stating that it had completed its investigation and determined that an error didnt occur, based on a thorough and reasonable investigation, and that the {$490.00} temporary credit would be reversed on XX/XX/XXXX. This notice did not explain why the merchants written instructions and refund acknowledgment were not sufficient, did not identify any missing evidence, and did not provide any meaningful basis for the denial beyond generic conclusory language. After speaking with a USAA customer service representative, I reopened the dispute on XX/XX/XXXX and made sure again that all necessary documentation had been provided. On that same day, I received an electronic document from USAA acknowledging that my request to reevaluate the dispute had been received and advising me to allow up to 30 business days for review. However, that same day, I also received another electronic document from USAA stating that the information requested to continue the investigation on my authorized transaction was not received or was insufficient, and that for that reason the investigation was complete and the dispute was closed. These same-day conflicting notices are deeply concerning. One message indicated the matter was under reevaluation, while another stated it had already been closed for lack of information. I had already submitted the supporting documents, and no one from USAA was able to identify what additional information, if any, was supposedly missing. From that point forward, I called USAA every week to check the status, verify that all documentation had been received, and ask whether anything further was needed from me. According to my records, I contacted USAA on XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, XX/XX/XXXX, and XX/XX/XXXX. During these calls, I consistently attempted to cooperate in good faith, provide whatever was necessary, and obtain a meaningful explanation of what was preventing resolution. No one was able to explain why my documentation was insufficient, what specifically was missing, or why the dispute continued to be denied. On XX/XX/XXXX, I filed a formal complaint by phone with a USAA customer service representative and was told I would receive a call from a representative. I never received that call. On XX/XX/XXXX, I called again and was told essentially the same thing. That representative advised me that if I did not hear back by the following week, I should request a Member Resolution Team. On XX/XX/XXXX, I received yet another electronic document from USAA stating that it had completed its investigation and determined that an error didnt occur after a complete review of internal records and relevant information. The same day, I received another document again saying that USAA had received my request to reevaluate the dispute and that I should allow up to 30 business days for review. I did not make another reevaluation request that day. It appeared that USAA internally generated or attributed another request to me, while simultaneously sending a denial and another pending-review notice. This inconsistent handling made it impossible for me to understand the true status of my dispute. Following that, I contacted USAA and requested the Member Resolution Team. During that call, I again went through the full history of the dispute. The Member Resolution Team representative could not explain what was wrong with my claim, could not tell me what additional documentation was needed, could not provide any notes from the dispute team explaining the denial, could not see my prior formal complaint, and could not see the prior calls or notes that should have existed from my repeated contacts. The representative also could not provide a meaningful resolution beyond telling me to wait another 30 days. In effect, I was placed into a repeated cycle where my dispute was reopened, left pending without communication, then denied using generic language, with no one able to explain the reasoning and no accessible internal record of the prior handling. To be clear, I have proof of the parking transaction, proof of the charges, proof of the merchants written acknowledgment that I am owed a {$490.00} refund, and proof that the merchant specifically instructed me to pursue that amount through my bank dispute process because the merchant could not issue the refund directly. This was not a speculative claim. It was supported by direct written communication from the merchant and by my transaction records. Despite that, USAA has now put me through multiple dispute cycles without meaningful review, explanation, or resolution. My concerns are not limited to the outcome itself. I am also concerned by the broader way USAA handled this matter. Specifically : USAA repeatedly issued generic denial notices without identifying the factual or procedural basis for denial. USAA sent conflicting notices on the same day indicating both that my dispute was being reevaluated and that it was closed. USAA repeatedly claimed information was missing or insufficient, yet no representative could tell me what information was lacking. USAA failed to maintain or surface internal records of my repeated calls, formal complaint, and prior dispute-handling notes in a way that allowed the issue to be effectively reviewed. USAA failed to provide me with access to anyone who could actually explain the banks reasoning or resolve the matter. USAA effectively forced me into a repetitive 30-business-day cycle with no substantive communication and no meaningful progress. As a result of this process, I have lost significant time, have been forced to repeatedly revisit the same issue over several months, and have been denied a refund that the merchant itself acknowledged I am owed. I have been a USAA member since XXXX, and this experience has completely undermined my confidence in the banks dispute resolution process. I respectfully request that the CFPB require USAA to do the following : First, conduct a genuine and substantive review of my dispute by a qualified team with access to all submitted documents, prior calls, complaint history, and internal notes. Second, provide a clear written explanation identifying the precise reason the bank believes my dispute does not qualify, including how USAA evaluated the merchants written acknowledgment that I am owed {$490.00} and that the refund had to be handled through the dispute process. Third, process and credit the {$490.00} dispute amount consistent with the written documentation from the merchant. Fourth, investigate why USAA repeatedly issued contradictory notices, why internal complaint and call records were not visible to its own escalation personnel, and why no representative was able to tell me what was supposedly missing from my submission. Fifth, review whether USAAs dispute practices in this matter comply with applicable consumer protection and dispute-handling obligations, particularly where a consumer provides direct written evidence from a merchant confirming a refund is owed and must be resolved through the bank. I made every reasonable effort to resolve this directly with USAA before filing this complaint. I timely disputed the charge, submitted the requested documents, reopened the matter multiple times, called repeatedly to verify status and documentation, filed a formal complaint internally, and escalated to the Member Resolution Team. Despite all of that, USAA has provided no meaningful explanation and no resolution.

Consumer complaint narrative: FORMAL CFPB COMPLAINT REGULATION CC VIOLATIONS, FAILURE TO ACCOUNT FOR FUNDS, MISREPRESENTATION, AND ARBITRARY ACCOUNT CLOSURE I am submitting this complaint against Bank of America for multiple violations involving improper funds handling, failure to provide required disclosures, contradictory transaction reporting, and arbitrary account closure following my attempts to obtain lawful information. I. MATERIAL FACTS AND DOCUMENTED EVIDENCE On XX/XX/year>, I deposited XXXX checks in the amount of {$6000.00} each into my checking account. At the time of deposit, I was explicitly informed that no hold would be placed. This representation was relied upon and materially influenced my decision to proceed with the transaction. Later that same day, holds were applied retroactively and inconsistently, accompanied only by vague explanations including pending funds verification and refer to maker. At no point was I provided with a specific, factual basis identifying any defect, insufficiency, alteration, or fraud indicator associated with the checks. I independently confirmed with XXXX XXXX, the paying bank, that the funds were debited and the checks cleared without issue. This was further verified directly with the maker of the checks, whose account was charged the same day the checks were issued. I possess documentary evidence, including screenshots, confirming that the funds were available, debited, and not subject to return for insufficient funds or stop payment. Despite this, Bank of America later asserted that the checks were returned unpaid with a Refer to Maker designation. However, no documentary evidence has been provided to support this claim, including : No return transaction record No interbank return trace No return settlement confirmation No evidence that funds were transmitted back to the issuing bank This creates a direct contradiction between financial institutions and establishes a failure by Bank of America to properly account for the disposition of deposited funds. II. REGULATION CC VIOLATIONS Under Regulation CC 229.13 ( e ), a bank may invoke an exception hold only where it has reasonable cause to believe a check is uncollectible, and such determination must be based on specific, articulable facts. Bank of America failed to provide any such facts. Further, 229.13 ( g ) requires that when an exception hold is applied, the bank must provide a clear and specific statement of the reason for the delay, sufficient to allow the customer to understand the basis for the action taken. Statements such as pending verification and refer to maker are conclusory and do not meet the specificity requirement mandated by regulation. Additionally, 229.16 ( c ) requires that disclosures be clear, conspicuous, and meaningful. The explanations provided were vague, non-informative, and prevented any meaningful understanding or verification of the banks actions. III. FAILURE TO ACCOUNT FOR FUNDS / TRANSACTION DISCREPANCY Bank of America has asserted that the checks were returned unpaid while the issuing bank has confirmed no such return occurred. This contradiction, combined with the absence of any trace documentation, establishes a failure to properly reconcile or account for the funds. A banks obligation is not satisfied by assertion alone. It must be supported by verifiable transaction records. The failure to produce such documentation raises serious concerns regarding internal controls, reconciliation accuracy, and the handling of customer deposits. IV. MISREPRESENTATION AND UNFAIR PRACTICES At the time of deposit, I was informed that no hold would be placed. This statement was later contradicted by subsequent actions. This constitutes a material misrepresentation. Further, the use of vague, non-specific explanations, combined with contradictory statements regarding the status of the funds, constitutes an unfair and deceptive practice that prevented me from understanding or protecting my financial position. V. DENIAL OF INFORMATION AND OBSTRUCTION During multiple attempts to resolve this matter : Representatives refused to provide specific information Stated no additional details were available Refused escalation to a supervisor Terminated calls when escalation was requested Refused to provide identifying information This conduct interfered with my ability to obtain information regarding my funds and demonstrates a failure to provide reasonable access to account-related information. VI. ARBITRARY AND POTENTIALLY RETALIATORY ACCOUNT CLOSURE Following my repeated attempts to obtain information and escalate the issue, my account was closed with the sole explanation that my account activity put the bank at risk, with no factual basis provided. While banks may close accounts, the timing and circumstances of this closureimmediately following my efforts to question and escalateraise serious concerns that the action was arbitrary and potentially retaliatory in nature. The refusal to provide any explanation further compounds concerns regarding transparency and fairness. VII. DISPARATE AND UNPROFESSIONAL TREATMENT On XX/XX/year>, at a branch in XXXXXXXX XXXX, I was treated in a dismissive and demeaning manner by a branch manager who explicitly stated she did not have to answer my questions. During the same visit, I observed other customers receiving polite and cooperative assistance. Additionally, during a subsequent call, a representative identified as XXXX refused to provide identification, laughed when I requested escalation, and terminated the call. This pattern reflects inconsistent treatment and a failure to uphold professional standards. VIII. DEMAND FOR REGULATORY ACTION Based on the foregoing, I am requesting : Immediate investigation into the handling and disposition of my deposited funds Production of all transaction records, including any alleged return documentation A formal check trace and reconciliation review Determination of compliance with Regulation CC Review of internal controls and decisioning processes Correction of any inaccurate reporting or account records Accountability for failure to provide required disclosures CONCLUSION This matter involves more than a routine deposit dispute. It reflects a systemic failure to provide required disclosures, properly account for funds, and maintain transparency in customer transactions. The inability to reconcile contradictory statements between banks, combined with the absence of documentary proof and the refusal to provide information, raises serious concerns that warrant immediate regulatory intervention. I respectfully request that this matter be reviewed with urgency and that corrective action be taken.

Consumer complaint narrative: RE : Supplemental/Related Complaint Against Chime Financial , Inc . Continued EFTA Violations, Pattern of Bad-Faith Dispute Handling, and Failure to Respond to Formal Demand Original Complaint ID : XXXX Dear Consumer Financial Protection Bureau , I am writing to supplement and renew my previously filed complaint ( ID # XXXX ) against Chime Financial, Inc. ( Chime ) in connection with unauthorized fraudulent transactions totaling approximately {$400.00} that were made on my account without my knowledge or authorization. This supplemental complaint is necessitated by a continuing pattern of conduct by Chime that I believe constitutes clear and repeated violations of the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( EFTA ), 15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq., and Regulation E, 12 C.F.R. Part 1005. Since my initial complaint, the situation has materially worsened. I respectfully request that the Bureau treat this correspondence as a related and supplemental complaint to my prior filing, and that it be incorporated into Chimes ongoing regulatory record. I. Background and Prior Complaint On or about the date of the XX/XX/year>, I discovered approximately {$400.00} in unauthorized charges on my Chime account. I reported the fraud to Chime within approximately one hour of discovering the transactions well within the reporting windows established under the EFTA. I also filed a police report documenting the fraud and provided Chime with a copy. Despite this, Chime denied my initial dispute. I filed a second dispute, which was also denied. Following those denials, I filed a formal complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, a complaint with the Better Business Bureau, and sent formal written Notice of Demand letters to Chime Financial , Inc. via XXXX mail on XX/XX/year>, citing violations of the EFTA and demanding reimbursement. Chime never responded to those demand letters. II. New and Continuing Violations Since Initial Complaint Since the filing of my initial CFPB complaint, Chimes conduct has continued in a manner that strongly suggests bad faith, automated processing, and willful disregard of federal law. The following events have occurred and form the basis of this supplemental complaint : 1. Chime independently reopened one of my disputes on its own initiative and denied it within 24 hours, providing no written explanation of its findings. A meaningful investigation of a fraud dispute can not be completed in 24 hours. This conduct is facially inconsistent with the reasonable investigation standard required under 15 U.S.C. 1693f and 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( c ). 2. Chime also independently reopened a second, separate dispute and denied it as well, again without providing a written explanation of findings or the basis for denial. 3. Chime has failed to provide me with written findings explaining the basis of any of its denials. Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( d ), when a financial institution determines no error occurred, it must promptly deliver a written explanation of its findings and inform the consumer of the right to request the documents it relied upon. 4. Chime failed to respond to XXXX XXXX mail demand letters sent on XX/XX/year> to its principal address at XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX. These letters cited the EFTA by statute, included my police report, and provided a deadline for response. No response was ever received. 5. In total, I have now been denied reimbursement XXXX times across XXXX separate disputes. The pattern of conduct rapid automated denials, failure to explain findings, failure to respond to formal legal demands, and failure to conduct genuine investigations suggests systemic noncompliance rather than isolated error. III. Applicable Legal Standards The EFTA and Regulation E impose specific obligations on financial institutions that handle electronic fund transfers on behalf of consumers. Under 15 U.S.C. 1693f and 12 C.F.R. 1005.11, when a consumer reports an unauthorized electronic fund transfer, the financial institution must : ( 1 ) investigate the claim within 10 business days ( or issue a provisional credit while conducting a longer investigation of up to 45 days ) ; ( 2 ) conduct a reasonable, good-faith investigation of the alleged error ; ( 3 ) provide written notice of its findings upon completion ; and ( 4 ) inform the consumer of their right to request the documents relied upon in the determination. Under 15 U.S.C. 1693g, the burden of proof rests with the financial institution to establish that the transfer was authorized. Chime has not met any of these obligations. It has not conducted reasonable investigations, has not provided written findings, has not offered provisional credit, and has not met its burden of proving authorization.

Additionally, similarity to prior activity is not a valid basis to deny a claim under Regulation E when unauthorized access is reported. SoFi also failed to provide a meaningful explanation of their investigation. Their response does not indicate whether they reviewed : - Device access logs - IP address or geolocation data - Merchant authentication records- XXXX XXXX transaction verification data Instead, they provided only generalized conclusions without describing the investigative steps taken, which does not meet Regulation Es requirement for a reasonable, good-faith investigation. I am requesting that : 1. SoFi reopen and reinvestigate all disputed transactions collectively as part of a single unauthorized event 2. SoFi provide a detailed explanation of the investigative steps taken for each transaction 3. Any improperly denied transactions be reimbursed in accordance with Regulation E I am seeking a fair and compliant resolution to this matter. I am writing to file a formal complaint against Charles Schwab XXXX regarding the unauthorized suspension of my checking account and the unlawful withholding of approximately {$2000.00} in deposited funds. BACKGROUND In late XX/XX/year>, I opened a joint checking account with Charles Schwab XXXX. The account was fully approved and operational. Over the following weeks, I engaged in normal banking activities, including : - Receiving direct deposit payments from two employers into the account - Writing checks that were processed and cleared - Receiving and activating debit cards for both account holders- Sending a wire transfer from the account to my XXXX XXXX XXXX account At no point during or after account opening was I asked to provide additional identity verification. Schwab accepted my deposits, issued debit cards, processed checks, and facilitated a wire transfer all of which require identity verification under federal banking regulations. THE INCIDENT On or about XX/XX/year>, I attempted to send a XXXX transfer through the Schwab platform. The transfer failed. I contacted Schwab customer support through their website, and was told the failure was due to an internal problem with XXXX not an issue on my end. Shortly after, my entire account was locked without warning. I was unable to log in online, and both debit cards associated with the account were deactivated. I received no prior written notice no letter, no email, no phone call informing me of any issue with my account or giving me an opportunity to address any concerns before access was revoked. When I called Schwab customer service, I spent approximately XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX on the phone being transferred between representatives, placed on hold repeatedly, and given conflicting information. I was told : - My account had been flagged for identity verification due to the failed XXXX transfer and unspecified " other things '' that the representative refused to disclose. - I was required to provide a notarized Letter of Authorization a form I was expected to create myself, as Schwab does not provide one. - I was required to provide a government-issued photo ID ( front and back ), verification of deposits ( check stubs ), and a current mortgage statement or utility bill as proof of address. - I was initially told to visit a Schwab branch in person. The nearest branch is in XXXX, Tennessee approximately XXXX XXXX from my home. The representative later told me I couldnt use this branch because it is independent. My own research revealed the nearest company branch is in XXXX, Tennessee, over XXXX XXXX from my home. When I explained this was not feasible, I was told I could use an online notary instead. - The supervisor could not confirm when my account would be restored after I submitted the required documents. She stated only that the matter would be " escalated '' and a manager would follow up the next day. HARM AND IMPACT As a result of Schwab 's actions, I have suffered the following harm : - I am unable to access approximately {$2000.00} of my own money, which includes wages deposited by my employers. - I am unable to pay contractors I have hired for essential services related to my upcoming move. - I am XXXX and live in rural Tennessee with limited transportation. Traveling to the nearest Schwab branch or a notary public is not feasible. - I lost an hour and a half of productive work time during the phone call, during which I had urgent professional deadlines. - I experienced significant emotional distress, including chest, as a direct result of being told I could not access my own money. - I am in the process of relocating internationally and closing on the sale of my home. This account disruption has jeopardized my ability to manage my finances during this critical transition. SPECIFIC COMPLAINTS 1. Schwab accepted deposits, processed checks, issued debit cards, and facilitated a wire transfer before requiring identity verification. If verification was required, it should have been completed at account opening before funds were deposited, not after. 2. Schwab locked my account without any prior written notice. I received no letter, email, or other communication informing me of a pending issue or giving me an opportunity to resolve it before my access was revoked. 3. Schwab is requiring me to create my own notarized verification form rather than providing a standardized document. This is an unreasonable burden on a consumer and suggests a lack of proper procedures. 4. Schwab could not provide a timeline for restoring my access to my own funds, even after I comply with their verification requirements. 5. Schwab refused to disclose the specific reasons for flagging my account beyond the failed XXXX transfer, citing vague " security '' concerns while simultaneously holding my money hostage. 6. The requirement to visit a branch in person discriminates against consumers in rural areas who do not have reasonable access to a physical branch location. SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION I am attaching the following evidence in support of this complaint : - Screenshot of Schwab mobile app login error showing account suspension - Screenshot of Schwab website login error requiring identity verification - Payment stubs from employers showing direct deposits to the Schwab account I am prepared to provide additional documentation upon request. I expect to follow up on this complaint once my account access is restored and I can confirm the full extent of the disruption. I am filing this complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau because I believe Schwab 's conduct violates my rights under federal consumer financial protection laws. A federally insured banking institution should not be permitted to accept deposits, issue debit cards, process checks, and facilitate wire transfers and then, weeks later, lock a consumer out of their own funds without prior notice, without providing a standardized verification process, and without any guaranteed timeline for restoring access. This practice effectively holds consumer funds hostage and causes severe financial and emotional harm.

Further, the failure to determine whether these debits were properly authorized raises concerns as to whether these transactions were properly payable under applicable law. I am formally requesting that KeyBank : -Produce the complete ACH authorization ( signed, recorded, or otherwise verifiable ) permitting XXXX XXXX XXXX AP to debit my account -Provide a detailed account of its investigation, including all steps taken to verify authorization -Reimburse all debits if valid authorization can not be produced If KeyBank is unable to produce valid authorization, its continued refusal to reimburse these transactions raises significant concerns regarding compliance with consumer protection obligations governing electronic fund transfers. Yet the bank simultaneously stated that it had placed a " temporary hold '' on the deposit " to protect both you and the bank in the event the check was returned unpaid. '' These two statements are logically contradictory. A hold, by definition, restricts access to deposited funds. If the funds were truly available on XX/XX/XXXX, then there was no hold and my complaint was entirely unfounded. If a hold was placed, then I was deprived of timely access to my funds, and the bank 's denial of my reimbursement request is unjustified. What specific harm did this cause? Regulation CC sets forth specific time schedules that banks must follow when making deposited funds available to consumers, and requires banks to clearly disclose their funds availability policies. The EFAA was enacted to reduce the time that banks could hold deposited checks, and Regulation CC establishes federal standards for when banks must make deposited funds available and how hold policies must be disclosed. Bank of America 's contradictory statements regarding this deposit suggest that the bank either : 1. Placed an unauthorized hold without proper disclosure, in violation of Regulation CC ; or 2. Made the funds available as required, in which case the bank 's initial hold was improper and the bank 's refusal to explain what occurred constitutes a deceptive practice. Consumer complaint narrative: Complaint Against Bank of America , N.A . Issue : Unauthorized ACH Transfers/ Failure to Protect Deposited Funds Amount at Issue : Approximately {$8000.00} Summary of Complaint Bank of America , N.A . failed to implement and maintain reasonable information security, customer data protection, and fraud detection controls, which directly resulted in multiple unauthorized ACH transactions being fraudulently withdrawn from my checking account. Despite timely reporting, Bank of America has failed to reimburse me for approximately {$8000.00} in stolen funds, causing significant financial harm. Description of What Happened My Bank of America checking account was compromised due to Bank of Americas failure to adequately protect my account and monitor for fraudulent activity. A single perpetrator was able to initiate multiple unauthorized ACH transfers, in rapid succession, to the same payee. These transactions were executed without my knowledge, authorization, or consent. At no point did Bank of America : - Notify me of suspicious or anomalous transaction activity, - Intervene to suspend or block the transactions, or - Apply basic velocity controls or ACH fraud safeguards that are standard within the banking industry. These transactions occurred openly and repeatedly, demonstrating a total breakdown in Bank of Americas fraud monitoring and customer protection systems. The first and only notification I received of this activity was when my account has withdrawn. Failure of Information Security and Customer Data Protection Bank of America holds itself out as a financial institution capable of safeguarding customer funds and sensitive financial data. In this instance, Bank of Americas information security and customer data protection programs failed. Unauthorized access to my account was possible, and once compromised, the account remained vulnerable long enough for multiple fraudulent transfers to be completed. This failure constitutes a breakdown in Bank of Americas obligations to implement reasonable administrative, technical, and operational safeguards to protect consumer accounts. Failure of Fraud Detection and ACH Controls The unauthorized activity exhibited obvious fraud indicators, including : - Multiple ACH transfers occurring in a short period of time, - Transfers sent to the same payee, - Transaction behavior inconsistent with my historical account usage. Any reasonable ACH monitoring system employing standard velocity limits, anomaly detection, or transaction pattern analysis should have flagged and prevented this activity. Had Bank of America implemented effective fraud detection controls, the theft would have been interrupted early, and my financial losses would have been negligible. Instead, Bank of America allowed the perpetrator to continue withdrawing funds unchecked. Resulting Harm As a direct and proximate result of Bank of Americas failures : - Approximately {$8000.00} was fraudulently removed from my checking account. - I am unable to meet existing financial obligations. - I have suffered financial hardship caused solely by Bank of Americas failure to safeguard funds I entrusted to them. - Bank of America has failed to reimburse the stolen funds timely despite the transactions being unauthorized. Bank of Americas Responsibility Bank of America was the entity that : - Controlled the account infrastructure, - Processed the ACH transactions, - Failed to detect and prevent repeated fraudulent withdrawals, and - Allowed the continued removal of my funds after clear fraud indicators were present. The loss was caused by Bank of Americas deficient fraud prevention framework, not by any wrongdoing or negligence on my part. Requested Resolution I respectfully request that the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau : - Require Bank of America to immediately reimburse me for the full amount of unauthorized withdrawals ( approximately {$8000.00} ). - Investigate Bank of Americas ACH transaction monitoring, velocity controls, and fraud detection systems that allowed repeated unauthorized transfers. - Require Bank of America to assess and strengthen its customer data protection and fraud prevention programs to prevent similar consumer harm. Closing Statement Consumers are entitled to rely on financial institutions to protect deposited funds through reasonable security and fraud control measures. Bank of America failed to meet this obligation and has improperly shifted the financial consequences of its failures onto me. CFPB intervention is necessary to ensure reimbursement and to prevent recurrence.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am disputing multiple unauthorized international debit card transactions that posted to my account on XX/XX/year>. I did not authorize these transactions, did not add my card to any digital wallet, and did not receive any goods or services from the merchants involved. These transactions occurred in multiple different countries, yet several of them had identical or nearly identical amounts, which is a common indicator of cardtesting fraud. The merchants were unrelated and located in different regions, and the repeated amounts are not consistent with legitimate use. I immediately reported the charges to the bank and submitted a written dispute. After I sent my dispute letter, the bank restricted my account access, preventing me from viewing my transaction history or communicating through normal channels. This restriction occurred only after I challenged the transactions, and it appears retaliatory. The bank did not conduct a proper investigation as required under Regulation E. Instead of contacting the merchants or obtaining documentation showing authorization, delivery of goods, or proof of benefit, the bank relied solely on internal tokenprovisioning screenshots. These logs do not prove that I authorized the transactions, do not show merchant responses, and do not demonstrate that I received anything of value. The only letter the bank sent me was written in an accusatory tone, implying that I had added my card to a digital wallet and authorized the transactions. This is not true, and the bank provided no evidence to support this claim. The letter did not include any merchant documentation, did not explain how they reached their conclusion, and did not meet Regulation Es requirement for a written explanation with supporting evidence. When I asked the bank to contact the merchants or provide merchant documentation, they told me they do not have the merchants contact information because the transactions were international. This is not accurate. Banks have access to merchant contact channels through the card network and the acquiring bank. Claiming they lack merchant contact information is a known indicator of a deficient investigation. When I requested a proper investigation and asked for the documentation used in their decision, the bank also told me that they are not required to reinvestigate any claim that has been closed as denied. They then stated they would look at the matter again as a courtesy. This is misleading. Regulation E requires a bank to reopen or reconsider a claim when the consumer provides new information, disputes the adequacy of the investigation, or requests the evidence used in the decision. A reinvestigation is not a courtesy ; it is a legal requirement when the initial investigation was incomplete or noncompliant. I repeatedly requested the full investigation file, including merchant documentation, chargeback responses, fraud case notes, and any evidence used to deny my claim. The bank refused to provide these materials. They also failed to respond to my written dispute letter and did not address the issues I raised. These actions reflect several known weaknesses that XXXX banks are frequently cited for : - relying on internal token logs instead of merchant evidence - refusing to obtain documentation from the acquiring bank - claiming they do not have merchant contact information - failing to provide required written explanations- failing to provide copies of evidence used in the decision - restricting or blocking customer accounts after a dispute is filed - ignoring written disputes and failing to respond within required timelines - mischaracterizing unauthorized transactions as authorized without proof- incorrectly claiming they do not have to reinvestigate a denied claim - treating required compliance steps as courtesies The banks failure to investigate, failure to obtain merchant documentation, failure to provide required evidence, refusal to reinvestigate, and failure to respond to my written dispute violate Regulation Es requirements for timely investigation, written findings, and supporting documentation. I am requesting that the CFPB require the bank to conduct a complete and compliant investigation, provide all documentation used in their decision, restore my account access, and refund the unauthorized transactions.

Incentives should be structured in a way that also benefits people who are trying to get started or rebuild financially. Consumer complaint narrative: Huntington National Bank ( Huntington ) has ( 1 ) placed successive holds on a single check deposit in a manner inconsistent with the Expedited Funds Availability Act ( EFAA ), 12 U.S.C. 4001 et seq., and its implementing Regulation CC, 12 C.F.R. Part 229 ; and ( 2 ) denied me access to a credit product ( XXXX XXXX ) based on overdraft activity that does not appear in my account transaction history, without providing the itemized basis for that adverse determination upon request. XXXX. Facts XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, I deposited a check in the amount of {$5300.00} into my Huntington Perks Checking account ending in XXXX/ nicknamed XXXX. XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX sent an automated email titled Hold Placed on Deposit stating that the {$5300.00} deposit was not available for immediate withdrawal and that [ a ] hold was placed on the deposit through XX/XX/XXXX. The notice provided no statutory reason for the hold as required under 12 C.F.R. 229.13 ( g ) ( exception hold notice ) or 229.16 ( case-by-case hold notice ). XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX sent a second automated email titled Deposit Hold Released confirming that [ w ] eve released the hold on a check deposit dated XX/XX/XXXX for {$5300.00}. XXXX. On XX/XX/XXXX, XXXX sent a third automated email titled Hold Placed on Deposit stating that the same {$5300.00} deposit was again not available for immediate withdrawal and that [ a ] hold was placed on the deposit through XX/XX/XXXX. Again, no statutory basis was identified. XXXX. As of XX/XX/XXXX, XXXXXXXX XXXX ET, my available balance was {$0.00}. The deposited funds remained inaccessible for approximately six calendar days following the original deposit date. 6. On a separate date, I called Huntington customer service to ( a ) request an explanation for the re-imposition of the hold after its release, and ( b ) request an itemized list of the three overdraft transactions Huntingtons mobile application cites as the basis for my ineligibility for Standby Cash. Huntington has not provided either. 7. Huntingtons Account Eligibility & More screen, last updated XX/XX/XXXX, states I am ineligible for Standby Cash because of 3 overdraft transactions in Huntington Perks CheckingXXXX in the last 96 days. A transaction search within the same Huntington application, filtered for Item Type Overdraft Payment across the date range XX/XX/XXXX through XX/XX/XXXX, returns No transactions found for the searched criteria. III. Legal Issues A. Regulation CC Funds Availability and Notice Requirements Under 12 C.F.R. 229.12, local check deposits are generally subject to next-business-day or second-business-day availability for the bulk of the funds. A depositary bank may extend availability under the exception holds enumerated at 12 C.F.R. 229.13 ( large deposits, new accounts, redeposited checks, repeated overdrafts, reasonable cause to doubt collectibility, emergency conditions ). The deposit at issue, {$5300.00}, falls below the {$5500.00} large-deposit threshold under 229.13 ( b ). When a bank invokes an exception hold, 229.13 ( g ) requires a written notice stating ( i ) the customers account number, ( ii ) the date and amount of the deposit, ( iii ) the amount being delayed, ( iv ) the reason the exception was invoked, and ( v ) the day funds will be available. Huntingtons notices identify the account, amount, and release date, but do not state the reason for the hold, in apparent noncompliance with 229.13 ( g ) ( 1 ) ( iv ). More significantly, Regulation CC does not contemplate the re-imposition of a hold on a deposit after the bank has affirmatively released that hold, absent a specific triggering event such as the check being returned unpaid by the paying bank in which case the banks obligations are governed by the returned-check provisions of 229.33 and the customer is owed a notice of nonpayment, not a silent re-hold. Huntington has provided no such notice and the deposit does not appear to have been returned. B. Adverse Action and Disclosure of Basis Huntingtons denial of Standby Cash credit based on a stated count of overdraft transactions that does not match the banks own customer-facing transaction records raises questions under ( i ) the accuracy obligations applicable to consumer credit decisions, and ( ii ) the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, 15 U.S.C. 1691 ( d ) and Regulation B, 12 C.F.R. 1002.9, which require creditors to provide a statement of specific reasons for adverse action upon a consumers request. I requested the specific basis ( the three transactions ) and Huntington declined to provide it.

Consumer complaint narrative: Complaint regarding improper denial of unauthorized transaction following an armed robbery XXXX XXXX transaction {$1500.00} SUMMARY I am filing this complaint on behalf of my business ( an LLC registered in XXXX ) against Bank of America regarding the improper denial of a fraud claim arising from an armed robbery in which my mobile phone was forcibly stolen at gunpoint. Bank of America has denied the claim based solely on evidence provided by XXXX XXXX showing that the transaction was executed from my own device the very device that was taken from me by armed perpetrators. Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005 ), use of a stolen device can not constitute authorization, and the burden of proof to demonstrate authorization rests with the financial institution. THIS COMPLAINT IS TIME-SENSITIVE. Bank of America has notified me in writing ( letter dated XX/XX/XXXX ) that the temporary credit of {$1500.00} will be removed from my account on XX/XX/XXXX. I respectfully request that CFPB process this complaint with appropriate urgency. THE ARMED ROBBERY ( XX/XX/XXXX ) On XX/XX/XXXX, at approximately XXXX XXXX local time, I was the victim of an armed robbery in XXXX, XXXX, while traveling as a passenger in an XXXX vehicle. XXXX perpetrators on motorcycles intercepted the vehicle. XXXX pointed a firearm at me and at the XXXX driver, while the other forcibly took my XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The phone was unlocked at the moment of the robbery because I was responding to a message. The phone contained my financial applications, including the Bank of America app and the XXXX XXXX app, with a saved Bank of America debit card as the payment method. THE UNAUTHORIZED TRANSACTION IN DISPUTE Approximately XXXX hour and XXXX minutes after the robbery, the perpetrators executed an unauthorized transaction using my stolen device : - Date/time : XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX XXXX - Amount : {$1500.00} USD - XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX - XXXX XXXX Case Number : XXXX - Payment method : Bank of America debit card ( ending XXXX XXXXXXXX ) - Beneficiary : a person unknown to me, in XXXX, receiving funds via XXXX XXXX XXXX - Bank of America Claim Number XXXX XXXX I did not authorize this transaction. I did not provide my PIN, banking credentials, XXXX XXXX credentials, or any form of permission to a third party. I did not consent to the use of my debit card. I do not know the beneficiary that person is not a contact, vendor, business partner, or service provider associated with my business or with me personally. CONTEXT : THE RELATED TRANSACTION FROM THE SAME CRIMINAL INCIDENT During the same robbery and from the same stolen device, the perpetrators also executed an unauthorized wire transfer of {$4900.00} USD on XX/XX/XXXX at XXXX XXXX ( Bank of America Claim Number XXXX ). After I submitted my formal appeal by fax on XX/XX/XXXX with the supporting documentation, Bank of America issued a credit of {$4900.00} to my account on XX/XX/XXXX, which remains credited to date with no further action by the bank. This is relevant because both transactions the {$4900.00} and the {$1500.00} were executed minutes apart, from the same stolen device, during the same criminal event documented by Colombian authorities. IT IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT FOR BANK OF AMERICA TO RECOGNIZE XXXX OF THESE TRANSACTIONS AS UNAUTHORIZED FRAUD WHILE SIMULTANEOUSLY CLASSIFYING THE OTHER AS AUTHORIZED. BANK OF AMERICA 'S DENIAL AND WHY IT IS IMPROPER On XX/XX/XXXX, Bank of America issued a letter stating : " The charge was authorized by you or made by someone who has permission to use the card or account. '' The letter indicates that the temporary credit of {$1500.00} will be removed on XX/XX/XXXX. This determination is legally and factually deficient for the following reasons : 1. DEVICE RECOGNITION IS NOT AUTHORIZATION. The denial relies on evidence showing the transaction was executed from my XXXX. This is not evidence of authorization it confirms that the perpetrators executed the fraud using my stolen, unlocked device, taken under threat of deadly force. Under 12 CFR 1005, use of a stolen device can not constitute consumer consent. If device recognition alone could defeat a fraud claim, no theft of an unlocked phone could ever result in consumer protection which is precisely the harm the statute is designed to prevent. 2. BANK OF AMERICA HAS THE BURDEN OF PROOF. Under 12 CFR 1005.6 and 1005.11, when a consumer reports an unauthorized electronic fund transfer, the financial institution bears the burden of demonstrating that the transfer was authorized. Bank of America has not provided evidence of authorization only evidence of device access. Under federal law, these are not the same thing. 3. THE XXXX XXXX " EVIDENCE '' DOES NOT ESTABLISH AUTHORIZATION. I obtained the chargeback response XXXX XXXX provided to Bank of America, and the documents themselves do not prove authorization : - The " Terms & Conditions Acceptance '' screenshot XXXX XXXX submitted only demonstrates that someone checked a box on my stolen phone. Anyone in possession of an unlocked phone can check a box. This is not consumer consent it is mechanical interaction with a screen by whoever physically holds the device. - The AVS ( Address Verification System ) match is not authorization either. The registered address was stored within my phone and accounts. The perpetrators had access to my phone where this information was saved. - The " transfer history '' XXXX XXXX submitted as supposed proof of legitimate use is inconsistent with the disputed transaction. It shows only XXXX prior transfer dated XX/XX/XXXX, for {$320.00} to a completely different beneficiary, using a completely different credit card. This single, much smaller, completely unrelated transaction does not establish a pattern of authorized behavior. On the contrary, it demonstrates that the disputed {$1500.00} transfer to a person I do not know is anomalous compared to my actual usage history. 4. THE TRANSACTION PROFILE IS CONSISTENT WITH FRAUD, NOT AUTHORIZED USE. - The transaction was executed within XXXX hour and XXXX minutes of an armed robbery documented by XXXX authorities ( criminal case number XXXX XXXX ). - The funds were sent to a beneficiary completely unknown to me. - The funds were sent to a XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX, a XXXX instant-payment service that allows rapid extraction of funds a method commonly used in post-theft fraud schemes precisely because it is difficult to recover. - The transaction occurred in immediate temporal proximity to a violent crime that I formally reported to law enforcement. 5. BANK OF AMERICA 'S OWN ACTIONS DURING THIS SAME INCIDENT CONTRADICT ITS DENIAL. During my initial call to report the fraud, Bank of America successfully intercepted and stopped additional unauthorized transaction attempts on my account. The bank itself recognized fraudulent activity in real time and took protective action. It is internally inconsistent for Bank of America to acknowledge fraud was actively occurring on the account while simultaneously concluding that the earlier transactions in the same fraud sequence executed minutes apart, from the same stolen device were authorized. 6. BANK OF AMERICA ALREADY RECOGNIZED THE FRAUD IN THIS SAME INCIDENT BY ISSUING A CREDIT FOR THE {$4900.00} TRANSACTION. As stated above, the bank issued a credit for the related {$4900.00} transaction executed minutes apart from the same stolen device. There is no legal or logical basis to treat the XXXX transactions differently both were executed by the same perpetrators, from the same stolen device, during the same criminal event. 7. I REPORTED WITHIN THE PROTECTED TIMEFRAME. I notified Bank of America within hours of the robbery, well within the timeframes established by Regulation E for maximum consumer protection. DOCUMENTED IMMEDIATE ACTIONS TAKEN - Filed an official police report with the XXXX XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXXXXXX in XXXX, obtaining criminal case number XXXX XXXX. - Requested IMEI block of the stolen device with my mobile carrier ( XXXX ) less than XXXX hours after the robbery. The device is also confirmed as BLOCKED in the public XXXX stolen-device registry and in XXXX XXXX 's IMEI block system. - Reported the fraud to Bank of America. During my initial call, the bank intercepted and stopped additional unauthorized transaction attempts. - Submitted a formal appeal package to Bank of America by fax on XX/XX/XXXX with all supporting documentation. - Provided detailed supplemental information to the Colombian Fiscala on XX/XX/XXXX, including precise location, time, beneficiary information, device specifications, and full transaction details. RESOLUTION REQUESTED I respectfully request that Bank of America : 1. Reverse the denial of the {$1500.00} claim. 2. Cancel the scheduled removal of the temporary credit on XX/XX/XXXX. 3. Permanently credit the {$1500.00} unauthorized XXXX XXXX transaction. 4. Reclassify the transaction as " unauthorized electronic fund transfer due to stolen device under armed robbery. '' 5. Apply the protections of the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1693 ) and Regulation E ( 12 CFR Part 1005 ), including the bank 's legal burden to demonstrate authorization rather than relying solely on device recognition. 6. Provide a written explanation that addresses the specific legal points above, rather than relying on automated device-recognition reasoning. The XXXX official documents are issued in XXXX, the official language of the jurisdiction where the crime occurred, and constitute valid official records of the criminal incident.

He instructed her to withdraw our entire savings of {$16000.00} in cash and redeposit it at a different Wells Fargo ATM on XXXX XXXX in XXXX XXXX, which was closed that Saturday. Here is what makes this story especially troubling : Wells Fargo has an ATM that accepted a {$16000.00} cash deposit and apparently diverted it to a fraudulent account. The bank should have video footage of my wife at that ATM, and a transaction record showing exactly where those funds went. Wells Fargo initially denied the existence of both. However, they finally released the photos, to the XXXX XXXX XXXX, of XXXX XXXX making the deposit but has not released the data showing the account that was credited. We reported the crime immediately to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( XXXX XXXX. XXXX ). Deputies were dispatched and went directly to the bank. Wells Fargo refused to provide transaction information to law enforcement. The Sheriff 's Office obtained a subpoena. As of now, the Sheriff 's Office has informed us that Wells Fargo has still not released the information. Detective XXXX XXXX, ( XXXX ) XXXX, is working the case but so far has only found the photos. He does not answer our calls but eventually returns them but shows no progress after XXXX months. We have met with branch officers multiple times. Nothing has been done. We have contacted XXXX attorneys, each of whom told us the case was not financially worth pursuing for them despite the severity of our loss. We are seniors. This money represented our security. We are not asking for sympathy we are asking for accountability. I believe this story raises serious questions that deserve public scrutiny : How did a bank ATM accept and redirect {$16000.00} in cash with no traceable record? I am writing to formally document a series of regulatory violations that occurred both today and yesterday at Bank of America financial XXXX # XXXX. As a business owner and the spouse of a 100 % XXXX veteran, I rely on the predictable liquidity of government funds. Bank of America has been our chosen financial institution for nearly XXXX years. Today, Bank of America failed to meet its statutory obligations under the Expedited Funds Availability Act ( EFA Act ). Statement of Facts : On XX/XX/year> at XXXX XXXX, I attempted to cash a state government warrant in the amount of {$2000.00}. I was informed that I may not cash the check but that I could deposit the check into my account and the funds would be available the following morning. An hour later I received a notice from my banking app that the check from the State Comptroller 's office which I had just deposited was now on a seven day hold. I immediately called customer service and was advised that the check was still processing and that they could only push the hold through if I called back the following day once the check had been processed. I waited until the following morning ( today ) and the check was still on hold. I attempted to speak with an associate on live chat through the official banking app with no success. I then visited branch # XXXX in person and requested the branch manager. Despite the check being a low-risk government item and well below the large-deposit threshold, the branch manager placed a multi-day hold on the funds. I remained in the branch for over 90 minutes seeking a resolution, which was summarily denied. Regulatory Violations : Violation of Mandatory Next-Day Availability ( 12 CFR 229.10 ( c ) ) : Under Federal Law, state government checks deposited in person to a staffed teller station must be made available for withdrawal not later than the business day after the banking day on which the funds are deposited. The branch 's refusal to provide next-day access is a direct breach of this mandate. Failure to Provide Statutory Notice of Exception ( 12 CFR 229.13 ( g ) ) : When a bank invokes an exception hold, it is legally required to provide the customer with a written notice at the time of deposit ( or by the next business day via mail ) stating the specific " Reasonable Cause '' for the hold. The branch manager explicitly refused my repeated requests for this documentation, stating incorrectly that general deposit disclosures were sufficient. Refusal to Verify Funds Requirement : I provided the bank with the Texas Comptrollers Warrant Status Inquiry System to verify the checks validity. The bank explicitly refused to perform this verification or acknowledge the proof of validity, claiming that they have internet Proxy Blockers on their computers and Private Branch Exchange telephone lines. I offered to call the State Comptrollers office on my personal telephone and they rejected my offer stating they could not verify the validity of the office Im calling. Misapplication of " Matching Funds '' Requirement : Branch staff informed me that the check would not be cashed because my account did not already contain the equivalent funds. Please be advised that Regulation CC contains no matching funds or recourse provision that overrides the mandatory availability of government warrants. Failure of Administrative Oversight : The branch refused to exercise its delegated authority to perform a manual override, citing an inability to reach internal departments, thereby penalizing the consumer for the banks internal operational failures.

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing a complaint against Bank of America for improperly denying my fraud claim and failing to comply with federal law. On XX/XX/2026, I disputed unauthorized electronic transactions totaling {$1200.00}. I did not authorize these transactions, did not provide consent, and did not receive any goods or services. Bank of America denied my claim based on the assertion that the transactions were authorized because they were conducted using my device and/or XXXX XXXX. This reasoning is legally insufficient. Under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act ( 15 U.S.C. 1693 ) and Regulation E ( 12 CFR 1005 ), an electronic fund transfer is considered authorized only if it is initiated with the consumers actual knowledge and express consent. The use of a device, IP address, passcode, or biometric authentication ( such as Face ID ) does NOT, by itself, establish authorization. Unauthorized use of a device even if it appears linked to the consumer does not meet the legal standard for authorization. Bank of America has failed to demonstrate that I provided valid consent for these transactions. They have also failed to provide sufficient evidence to support their conclusion, despite my request for documentation such as IP logs, device identification data, and merchant verification. Under 12 CFR 1005.11, the bank is required to conduct a reasonable and good-faith investigation. Denying my claim based solely on internal technical indicators, without proving actual authorization, does not satisfy this legal obligation. I am requesting the following : * Immediate reopening and escalation of my claim * Reimbursement of the full disputed amount of {$1200.00} * Full disclosure of all evidence used in the investigation, including technical and merchant records If this matter is not resolved promptly, I will pursue further action through regulatory enforcement channels and legal remedies.

I have since received IRS Notice XXXX confirming that the returned payment resulted in assessed penalties and interest. The IRS explicitly states that the penalty was charged because the bank did not honor the payment. The financial impact is : {$4000.00} dishonored payment penalty {$1000.00} failure-to-pay penalty {$630.00} interest Total damages to date : {$5700.00} This harm occurred despite sufficient funds being available and an overdraft protection feature being active. I am requesting that Citibank : Reimburse the full amount of IRS penalties and interest totaling {$5700.00} Review and correct how overdraft protection limitations are disclosed and operationalized, including providing real-time warnings or controls for transactions that exceed internal transfer limits Confirm corrective actions to prevent similar occurrences for other customers This issue is not simply a contractual dispute. Sub-issue: Account opened without my consent or knowledge
Consumer complaint narrative: I am submitting this complaint regarding Wells Fargos handling of my identity theft claim and their failure to comply with federal law requiring timely blocking of identity theft-related information. I notified Wells Fargo that I am a victim of identity theft concerning an account that was opened without my authorization. Despite this, Wells Fargo denied my claim on the basis that the account was opened using my personal information. This reasoning is fundamentally flawed. Identity theft, by definition, involves the unauthorized use of a consumers personal information. The mere use of accurate identifiers does not establish that I authorized this account. Additionally, Wells Fargo did not initially request or consider supporting documentation. At no point during the initial review was I asked to submit evidence such as an FTC Identity Theft Affidavit or any documentation supporting my claim. Only after I insisted that the matter be re-evaluated and offered to provide documentation did they show any willingness to consider additional information. This indicates that the original determination was made through automated or superficial verification methods rather than a meaningful investigation. The activity associated with my identity further supports my claim. Multiple accounts and credit applications were initiated within a very short timeframe, including the same day, across different institutions. This type of clustered activity is widely recognized as a strong indicator of identity theft and should have prompted a more thorough review. I have not benefited in any way from this account. I did not apply for, authorize, or use it, and I have no contractual relationship with Wells Fargo regarding it. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, identity theft information must be handled differently from standard disputes. Specifically, under * * 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 ( a ) * *, information resulting from identity theft must be * * blocked within four ( 4 ) business days * * upon receipt of proper notice. This is not subject to a standard reinvestigation timeline. Wells Fargos failure to properly address this claim and their reliance on superficial verification does not meet the legal standard required under federal law. Relevant case law reinforces these obligations : * * XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX * requires a reasonable and meaningful investigation * * XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. * prohibits reliance on automated verification without reviewing documentation * * XXXX XXXX XXXX & XXXX * establishes duty to properly investigate and correct inaccuracies * * XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX * requires removal of unverifiable information * * XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX superficial investigations * * XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX inaccurate information is a violation of the FCRA I have made a good faith effort to resolve this matter directly and have successfully had similar identity theft-related information removed by other institutions and consumer reporting agencies. This matter is serious and is not being taken lightly. The continued reporting and handling of this account is inconsistent with federal identity theft protections.

I received no call, so I proactively attempted to contact the Member Advocacy representative using the extension she provided in her email, and left multiple voicemail messages requesting a callback. I have still received no return calls or substantive follow-up communication from the Advocacy representative, nor anyone else from USAA regarding this matter. During one of the many calls with USAA, I raised a formal complaint by phone with USAA Member Resolution regarding the manner in which this matter was handled, which should be reflected in USAAs internal records. Despite doing so, I have received no substantive response or resolution to that complaint. Consumer complaint narrative: This complaint concerns J.P. Morgan/Chases refusal or failure to provide a consistent online method for customers to add or update beneficiaries for certain account types ( checking, savings ), while providing digital beneficiary-management functionality for other account categories ( XXXX XXXX XXXX ). Chases own beneficiary FAQ states that a beneficiary can be added to a Chase account by visiting a branch, while its investment materials separately state that customers with J.P. Morgan XXXX XXXX investment accounts can designate or update beneficiaries through the Chase Mobile app or on chase.com. The result is a fragmented and burdensome process in which customers may be required to appear in person for some accounts, even though the institution already maintains secure digital channels for beneficiary updates for other products. This discrepancy creates unnecessary friction in basic account administration and undermines efficient estate planning for deposit-account holders and similarly situated consumers. These interactions imposed avoidable time, travel, scheduling, and administrative burdens for a task that should be manageable through authenticated digital banking channels. Chases own public materials show that online beneficiary management is available for certain investment accounts, which demonstrates that the bank already has the operational capability to support remote beneficiary maintenance in at least part of its product ecosystem. The inability to update beneficiaries online is not a minor convenience issue. Beneficiary designations help assets pass directly to designated individuals and can reduce the probability of a drawn-out probate process. When a customer can not promptly complete or revise those designations, estate planning may be delayed, family expectations may remain unclear, and account administration at death may become more complicated than necessary. This issue is especially serious when customers are XXXX, XXXX, traveling, working irregular hours, managing family emergencies, or otherwise unable to appear at a branch easily. Requiring an in-person visit for a routine beneficiary update creates a disproportionate burden when comparable financial servicing functions are commonly handled through secure online and mobile channels, and when Chase itself already permits digital beneficiary updates for J.P. Morgan XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. J.P. Morgan/Chase appears to maintain different servicing standards depending on account type : branch-based beneficiary changes for at least some Chase accounts, but digital self-service for certain investment accounts. If the institution can authenticate customers and process beneficiary changes online for one class of accounts, it should be able to explain clearly why similarly sensitive changes for ordinary consumer deposit accounts require branch attendance rather than secure digital workflows, identity verification, and electronic acknowledgment. In addition, J.P. Morgan asset-management materials indicate that beneficiary designations for some non-qualified and IRA accounts are handled through paper forms submitted by mail, further illustrating that the customer experience varies significantly across account types and may depend on legacy processing channels rather than modern digital convenience. From a consumer-protection perspective, such inconsistency can cause confusion, delay, and needless effort in an area closely tied to end-of-life planning and family financial security. Consumer complaint narrative: You'll need a scrubbed version since they prohibit personal identifiers in the narrative. Here 's a clean paste, with name and account numbers stripped : On XX/XX/year>, Citibank returned a {$1700.00} ACH debit from my Citibank XXXX XXXX account that had presented against sufficient funds, while honoring a separate, larger ACH debit that posted hours later and actually overdrew the account. Citibank labeled the return as an insufficient funds event. It was not. It was a discretionary selection by Citibank to return the smaller, covered item rather than the larger, overdrawing one. The return is the type of high to low transaction handling that has been the subject of substantial consumer protection litigation and regulatory action against other large institutions. During my attempts to resolve the issue with Citibank by chat on XX/XX/year>, the escalation representative misrepresented the post-transaction balance, deflected with generic ACH definitions, and ultimately provided timestamps that confirmed the XXXX debit presented almost seven hours before the larger debit that overdrew the account. Citibank has nonetheless declined to reverse the return. FACTS As of XX/XX/year>, the available balance in the XXXX XXXX account was {$5600.00}. Citibank 's escalation representative confirmed this balance during the XX/XX/XXXX chat. Two ACH debits presented against the account on XX/XX/year> : a XXXX Bank personal loan payment of {$1700.00}, presented at XXXX XXXX, and a XXXX XXXX XXXX ACH debit of {$4000.00}, presented at XXXX XXXX. Both presentment timestamps were provided in writing by Citibank 's escalation representative. The XXXX item, standing alone, presented against an available balance of {$5600.00}. After the XXXX debit, the available balance was {$3900.00}. That figure also appears on Citibank 's own statement of account. The XXXX XXXX XXXX debit then presented almost seven hours later, against the post-XXXX balance of {$3900.00}, and exceeded it by {$150.00}. In other words, the XXXX item had coverage when it presented. The XXXX item did not. On XX/XX/year>, Citibank returned the XXXX debit, posting it as " Returned Insufficient Funds, ACH Txn '' for {$1700.00}. Citibank honored the larger XXXX XXXX XXXX debit that overdrew the account. Citibank selected the smaller item that had coverage when it presented and returned it, while paying the larger item that did not have coverage when it presented. At XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/year>, I transferred {$160.00} from my linked Citibank Checking account into the Savings Plus account, eliminating the negative balance the XXXX debit had created. The XXXX item itself had not required any additional funds, having presented against sufficient funds the prior day. The transfer is noted only to confirm that any negative balance on the account was brief and was self-cured by me from another Citibank account . THE CHAT WITH CITIBANK On XX/XX/year>, I contacted Citibank by chat. The chat first routed me through an automated assistant offering options that did not describe my issue. After the system did not produce a live agent, I had to type a direct demand before it would route me to a person. The first representative provided a generic explanation of how overdrafts work, then confirmed he could see in the account details that there had been sufficient funds for the XXXX item, but offered no resolution. When I requested escalation, he initially proposed only to forward my comments as feedback. When I insisted, he transferred the chat. The escalation representative made the following statements, all preserved in the chat transcript. First, he represented that the post-XXXX balance was negative {$150.00}, citing " our computerized records. '' That figure is the end of day balance after both XX/XX/XXXX debits had posted, not the balance after the XXXX item alone. The actual post-XXXX balance was {$3900.00}, as reflected on Citibank 's own statement and as the representative himself later confirmed in a transaction summary. Second, when I identified the error and asked why Citibank had selected the smaller, covered item for return rather than the larger overdrawing item, he responded with a paragraph defining ACH transactions and the statement that " Citi does not control the time of debiting the transaction. '' That statement does not address the discretionary return decision, which is made by Citibank, not by the ACH network. Third, he provided a transaction summary listing the XXXX XXXX XXXX debit as " Debit 1 '' and the XXXX debit as " Debit 2. '' Fourth, he then provided the presentment timestamps, which showed the XXXX debit presenting at XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX and the XXXX XXXX XXXX debit presenting at XXXX XXXX on XX/XX/XXXX. His own message therefore contradicts itself : he labeled the XXXX item as the second debit while simultaneously timestamping it as having presented almost seven hours before the item he labeled the first debit. Fifth, he offered to issue a " Transactions details letter confirming the time of ACH debits. '' I requested that letter. Sixth, after I noted that his own timestamps proved the XXXX item had presented first and had coverage, he attempted to walk back the timestamps, asserted that order of debit is " totally dependent on the ACH network, '' and re-cited the end of day available balance of negative {$150.00} as the operative figure. At no point did Citibank substantively address the central question : why Citibank chose to return the smaller item that had coverage at presentment and pay the larger item that did not. CONCERNS Citibank 's conduct raises concerns under the prohibition on unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices in three respects. First, mischaracterization of the return, since the bank labeled a discretionary return as an insufficient funds return when the item had presented against more than three times the available funds it required. Second, discretionary selection of the smaller covered item over the larger overdrawing item, which is the inverse of consumer protective transaction handling and tracks the high to low patterns that have produced substantial litigation and regulatory action against other large institutions. Third, misrepresentation of the operative balance figure during the complaint process, repeated even after I had identified the error and even after the bank 's own timestamps proved my position. DOWNSTREAM HARM The returned payment is a personal loan installment. The lender furnishes loan payment status to the major consumer credit bureaus. A 30 day late, which can be triggered by Citibank 's return, would result in adverse credit reporting and increased interest exposure beyond the late fee itself. The harm is concrete, foreseeable, and entirely a function of Citibank 's discretionary return decision.
