Consumer complaint narrative: I have been a Marcus savings account customer since XXXX. In XX/XX/XXXX, I became aware of a promotion offering a {$1500.00} bonus for depositing {$100000.00} in new funds and maintaining those funds in a Marcus account for 90 days. Because I already had an existing Marcus savings account, I contacted Marcus before moving any money to confirm that existing customers were eligible to participate in the promotion. After making that inquiry, I transferred {$100000.00} in new funds from XXXX into my Marcus savings account and maintained those funds for the required period. After more than 90 days had passed, I checked my account and discovered that the promised bonus had not been credited. When I contacted Marcus, I was informed that I was ineligible because I had not completed a separate enrollment process. The representative further stated that many customers had encountered the same issue. I escalated the matter to a supervisor, but again was told only that I had not enrolled and therefore would not receive the bonus. My complaint is not simply that I missed a procedural step. My concern is that the enrollment requirement appears to function as a barrier that predictably disqualifies consumers who otherwise satisfy the substantive requirements of the promotion. Marcus representatives themselves acknowledged that many customers fail to complete this step. If large numbers of consumers are being denied an advertised bonus for the same reason, that raises serious concerns about whether the requirement is being communicated effectively and transparently. As an existing customer, I was not opening a new account. I was responding to a promotional offer that required a deposit of new funds and a 90-day holding period. In that context, the term " enrollment '' was not presented to me as a critical requirement carrying a {$1500.00} consequence. The denial of a {$1500.00} bonus based solely on a missed procedural step is particularly troubling where the consumer has fully satisfied the economic substance of the promotion by depositing and maintaining {$100000.00} in new funds for the required period. What concerns me most is that the enrollment requirement serves no apparent substantive purpose. Marcus already knows when a customer deposits qualifying new funds and maintains those funds for the required period. If enrollment were truly intended to ensure informed participation rather than to create a procedural hurdle, Marcus could easily implement safeguards such as automatic prompts, warning messages before qualifying transfers, follow-up reminders, account notifications, or other mechanisms that would alert customers that an additional action is required. Instead, customers can deposit substantial sums, maintain those balances for months, and only later discover that they have been disqualified from receiving the advertised bonus. The practical effect of the current process is that XXXX receives the benefit of qualifying deposits while retaining the ability to deny the advertised bonus based on a procedural requirement that many consumers apparently overlook. Based on my experience and the number of similar complaints publicly reported by other consumers, this does not appear to be an isolated incident but rather a recurring source of consumer confusion. I have seen consumer complaints about this issue on CFPB, XXXX XXXX XXXX, XXXX, XXXX and other financial sites and social media. I attempted to resolve this matter directly with XXXX. I submitted a written complaint and sought reconsideration of my eligibility. Rather than addressing the substance of my concerns, Marcus repeatedly relied on the same response : that I had not enrolled. The bank did not address whether the enrollment requirement was adequately disclosed, whether the promotional process is reasonably understandable to existing customers, or whether recurring consumer confusion suggests deficiencies in the design or administration of the promotion. I respectfully request that this matter be reviewed to determine whether Marcus 's promotional practices, disclosures, and complaint-handling procedures are consistent with principles of fair and transparent treatment of consumers. I also request that Marcus reconsider its decision and honor the {$1500.00} promotional bonus based on my deposit of {$100000.00} in new funds and my compliance with the 90-day holding requirement. Thank you for your attention to this complaint.

Consumer complaint narrative: On XX/XX/year>, Robinhood notified me that my brokerage account would be closed and that my investment positions would be liquidated. Robinhood informed me that the proceeds would be returned to the bank accounts previously used to fund the account. The problem is that most of the funding accounts previously linked to my brokerage account are now closed and unavailable to receive returned funds. Robinhood either knew or should have known that attempting to send funds to closed accounts could create delays, confusion, and uncertainty regarding the location of customer assets. To date, I have received approximately {$2000.00} in XXXX active account that remains open. I have not received a complete accounting for the remaining proceeds from the liquidation of my investments. I do not know where the remaining funds are currently located, whether transfer attempts were made to closed accounts, whether those transfers were rejected, or what steps are being taken to return the remaining balance to me. The transaction history available to me does not clearly show the liquidation transactions, outgoing transfers, destination accounts, rejected transfers, or the current status of the remaining funds. As a result, I am unable to independently verify the location and status of my money. If Robinhood attempted to send funds to previously linked accounts, those transfer attempts and their outcomes should be clearly documented and visible to the customer. Customers should be able to see when funds were transferred, where they were sent, whether a transfer was successful or unsuccessful, and where the funds are currently being held if a transfer failed. Given that Robinhood currently has an active checking account linked to my profile, the most reasonable solution would have been to consolidate all liquidation proceeds into that active account. Alternatively, Robinhood should have provided me with the option to withdraw the funds myself or receive the remaining balance by check. Instead, funds appear to have been directed toward accounts that are no longer available, while I have not been provided with sufficient information to determine the status of my money. At this time, I have only been able to confirm receipt of approximately {$2000.00}. I can not determine where the remainder of the liquidation proceeds are located. This lack of transparency has caused significant concern and uncertainty regarding the handling of my assets. I am requesting that Robinhood provide a complete accounting of all liquidation proceeds, including the total amount liquidated, all transfer dates, destination accounts, any rejected transfers, and the current location and status of any funds that have not yet been returned to me. I am also requesting the prompt return of any remaining funds owed to me.

Consumer complaint narrative: I, XXXX XXXX, owner of XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, submit this complaint against Wells Fargo Bank N.A for its wrongful handling of a XXXX chargeback dispute ( reason code 10.4 - other fraud, card absent environment ) The financial harm to my business resulted from two distinct failures ; Wells Fargo 's failure to follow XXXX XXXX mandated dispute investigation procedures for card-not-present fraud and XXXX XXXX automatic deduction of transaction processing fees and dispute fees, which I was charged despite the dispute being incorrectly decided against me. Wells Fargo 's mishandling of this dispute led to an incorrect chargeback decision that caused direct and material financial harm to my business. MERCHANT ROLE IN THE TRANSACTION XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is a registered merchant operating on the XXXX XXXX platform, which uses XXXX as its payment processor. The following describes how transactions are processes in the environment, and why the merchant bears no responsibility for cardholder registration, verification or authorization. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX ( merchant ) has no involvement in bidder registration and does not handle, enter, or store any card credentials. The merchant does not perform and is not authorized to perform any verification, authentication, or authorization of payments. All cardholder data is transmitted directly and exclusively from the cardholder to XXXX. The merchant is never is possession of this information. Charges are processed and authorized automatically through XXXX 's secure, tokenized payment system entirely without merchant involvement. The merchant 's only visibility into a customer 's account is the name, billing and shipping addresses and last four digits of the card number - information already verified and authenticated by XXXX and the issuing bank prior to authorization. FACTS OF THE TRANSACTION On XX/XX/year> bidder XXXX XXXX registered on the XXXX XXXX platform. He purchased multiple lots of fine jewelry totaling {$3800.00}. Following the auction XXXX XXXX contacted XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX via email and requested that the items be shipped to the shipping and billing address on file with the XXXX XXXX platform. A shipping and insurance fee of {$120.00}. XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX fulfilled the order in the full compliance with platform procedures. The goods were delivered to the verified billing and shipping address provided by the buyer. The billing and shipping address were identical. On XX/XX/year> XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX received notice of a chargeback dispute for the full amounts of {$3800.00} and {$120.00}. All relevant evidence was promptly submitted to XXXX in response to the dispute. WELLS FARGO 'S DISPUTE DECISION ; On XX/XX/year> Wells Fargo issued its dispute decision in favor of the cardholder. The bank 's stated rationale was as follows : ( Our center has certified that this is an unauthorized transaction. The merchant provided no proof that our cardholder authorized the disputed transaction. Neither the name nor the address provided by the merchant matches our cardholder 's profile. The cardholder denies participation in the transaction, engagement with the merchant, or receipt of services. We have met all technical and certification requirements. The account was closed, placed on the exception file, and reported to XXXX as having been used fraudulently. Our cardholder is due full credit ) Wells Fargo categorized the dispute under XXXX Reason Code 10.4 ( other fraud card absent environment ) GROUNDS FOR COMPLAINT a ) The merchant XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX can not provide authorization proof. Wells Fargo 's decision faults the merchant for failing to provide proof that the cardholder authorized the transaction. This requirement is factually and procedurally impossible to satisfy. As described above, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX has no role in the authorization process. The merchant never handles card credentials, does not interact with XXXX or Wells Fargo 's authorization system, and is not provided with any authorization codes, CVV results, or AVS response coded. The information merchant submitted- the buyer 's name, billing and shipping address is the information that XXXX presented to Wells Fargo during the authorization request. If that information did not match Wells Fargo 's records, the bank had both the ability and the obligation to decline the transaction at the point of authorization. WELLS FARGO FAILED ITS DUTY AT THE POINT OF AUTHORIZATION Under XXXX Rules and XXXX Product and Service Rules, when an authorization request is submitted, the issuing bank is responsible for verifying cardholder credentials including name, billing address, and card validation codes against its own records. If those credentials do not match the issuer is required to return a decline response, such as Response Code 93 ( transaction can not be completed ) By approving the XXXX tokenized request, Wells Fargo effectively certified that the credentials presented were valid and acceptable. The bank can not now claim that the name and address did not match its records, while simultaneously having approved the transaction. These positions are mutually contradictory. The merchant had no mechanism to perform these checks and no access to the results of any AVS or CVV verification. Chargeback liability can not be assigned to a party who is structurally excluded from the authorization process. ASSIGNEMENT OF CHARGEBACK LIABILITY VIOLATES CARD NETWORK RULES XXXX XXXX own rules prohibit issuers from assigning chargeback liability to merchant under the following circumstances ; Merchants did not process or authorize the transaction. Merchant relied on processor level ( XXXX ) authentication and tokenization. The issuer approved the transaction through its own authorization system. FINANCIAL HARM FROM INCORRECTLY ASSESSED FEES In addition to the chargeback amount itself, XXXX automatically deducted transaction processing fees and dispute fees from my account in connection with these chargebacks. These fees were assessed despite the fact that the dispute was incorrectly decided and the merchant bore no responsibility. RELIEF REQUESTED XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX respectfully requests that the CFPB take the actions ; Direct Wells Fargo to reverse both chargebacks ( {$3800.00} and {$120.00} ), Direct Wells Fargo to reimburse all XXXX dispute fees assessed to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX as a result of this incorrectly decided dispute. I certify that the information in this complaint is true and accurate to the best of my knowledge. All supporting documentation will be submitted to this complaint. XXXX ( XXXX ) XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XX/XX/year> 2026

Consumer complaint narrative: I am filing this complaint regarding U.S. Bank 's systematic assessment of monthly service fees on a business checking account that was functionally unusable due to the bank 's own transfer restrictions. I opened a XXXX XXXX Checking Account on or about XX/XX/XXXX under my company : XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, intending to take advantage of a promotional offer requiring a {$25000.00} deposit. I had these funds readily available in my linked XXXX XXXX XXXX account. From the outset, U.S. Bank made funding the account impossible in any normal or routine manner : I was required to complete a manual PDF form just to deposit an initial {$300.00}. After linking my XXXX XXXX XXXX account ( which contained well over {$25000.00} ), U.S. Bank blocked external ACH transfers. I was informed by U.S. Bank employees that I could only fund the account through repeated small incremental transfersan impractical and burdensome process. I reasonably assumed that after depositing the {$300.00}, the linked XXXX XXXX XXXX account would allow the full {$25000.00} transfer. When this failed, I became frustrated and concluded the account was unusable for its intended purpose. I stepped away, reasonably believing my {$300.00} would remain safe until I could resolve the matter. U.S. Bank then assessed XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX monthly " dormancy '' fees * * against this account for over one year, systematically draining the entire {$300.00} balance and pushing the account to a negative balance. I received no noticeno mail, no email, no alertthat fees were accruing or that my balance was being depleted. When I discovered the negative balance, I immediately contacted U.S. Bank. They refunded only {$90.00} as a " courtesy '' ( actually only {$30.00} was refunded, not the {$90.00} they verbally claimed ), but refused to refund the remaining $ XXXX in fees. The bank 's own letter dated acknowledges the fees were charged and that they could reverse them, yet they have arbitrarily chosen not to fully reverse the wrongful charges. The bank 's advertising encouraged a {$25000.00} deposit with a cash bonus, while their systems made that deposit impossible. The bank then penalized me for inactivity on an account they made unusable. This is a bait-and-switch scheme that systematically traps consumers. Legal Violations A. Consumer Financial Protection Act ( CFPA ), 12 U.S.C. 5536 ( a ) ( 1 ) ( B ) U.S. Bank 's conduct constitutes an unfair, deceptive, or abusive act or practice ( UDAAP ) : Unfair Conduct : The bank knowingly imposed transfer restrictions that made the account unusable The bank assessed fees for inactivity while the account was unusable The bank provided no meaningful notice of accruing fees The bank 's $ XXXXmonth fee on a {$300.00} balance ( 10 % per month ) is disproportionate and causes substantial injury Deceptive Conduct : The bank advertised a bonus requiring a {$25000.00} deposit while making the required funding impossible The bank represented that linking an external account would enable transfers, then blocked them The bank 's letter acknowledges fees were " assessed correctly '' while also partially refunding themcontradictory representations The CFPB has previously fined U.S. Bank {$37.00} XXXX for similar misconductopening unauthorized accounts and engaging in deceptive sales practices. In that enforcement action, the CFPB found that U.S. Bank 's conduct caused " substantial injury to consumers in the form of fees, negative effects on credit reports, and the loss of control over their personal information ''. B. New Hampshire Consumer Protection Act ( RSA 358-A:2 ) Under New Hampshire 's Consumer Protection Act, it is unlawful to use " any unfair or deceptive act or practice in the conduct of any trade or commerce ''. Specifically, the statute prohibits : Claiming that goods or services have certain characteristics or benefits when they do not ( the bank advertised a bonus offer while making the {$25000.00} deposit impossible ) Falsely representing sponsorship, approval, status, or affiliation Advertising goods or services with the intent not to sell them as advertised The bank 's bonus offer was made with the intent to attract deposits, yet their systems were designed to block those deposits. This is precisely the type of deceptive conduct the NH Consumer Protection Act was designed to address. C. Truth in Savings Act ( 12 U.S.C. 4301 et seq. ) Banks are required to clearly and conspicuously disclose terms, fees, and charges. U.S. Bank 's fee structure $ XXXXmonth on a {$300.00} balancewas buried in fine print and not meaningfully disclosed. The bank 's $ XXXXmonth fee on a {$300.00} balance is 10 % per month120 % annuallyfar exceeding any reasonable service fee structure. The CFPB has noted that " dormancy fees, latency fees, or any other administrative fees or service charges that have the effect of reducing the total amount for which the holder may redeem '' are prohibited, and while this provision specifically addresses gift certificates, the same unfairness principles apply to bank dormancy fees. D. Implied Covenant of Good Faith and Fair Dealing Every contract includes an implied duty of good faith. U.S. Bank 's conductmaking the account unusable, charging fees for inactivity, and providing no noticeviolates this fundamental duty. The bank can not create the conditions that led to dormancy and then penalize the consumer for dormancy. U.S. Bank 's History of Misconduct : XX/XX/XXXX : The CFPB fined U.S. Bank {$37.00} XXXX for opening fictitious accounts without customer consent from XXXX to XXXX. The CFPB found the bank illegally accessed credit reports and opened checking, savings, credit card, and line of credit accounts without permission. I am asking the CFPB to investigate PNCs handling of this matter, including : 1. Why PNC refused to take account-level protective action after I reported active fraud and specifically asked for the account to be frozen ; 2. Why PNC allowed my paycheck to be used to offset a negative balance caused by transactions already reported and disputed as fraud ; 4. Whether PNCs handling of the provisional credit request complied with Regulation E and its obligations to consumers reporting unauthorized electronic fund transfers ; 5. They have failed to provide the legally demanded validation files, ignored explicit oral and written directives to cease collection activities, used deceptive local number spoofing tactics, transmitted unauthorized settlement text messages during an active dispute window, and engaged in telephonic harassment. Consumer complaint narrative: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Complaint Company : Wells Fargo Bank Related Claim ID : XXXX Related Executive Escalation Reference : XXXX Related CFPB Complaint Reference : XXXX Complaint Category : Investigation Process / Complaint Handling / Inconsistent Findings Complaint Narrative : This complaint concerns Wells Fargo 's handling of the investigation process itself and the changing factual basis used to support denial of my fraud claim. My original complaint involved unauthorized debit-card transactions totaling approximately {$15000.00} including resulting fees. However, the focus of this complaint is not simply the denial of reimbursement. Rather, it concerns the consistency, accuracy, and reliability of the investigative process utilized to reach that determination. Throughout the handling of the matter, Wells Fargo systems and representatives reflected materially different transaction counts and records. During the course of the investigation, I was presented with approximately 27 transactions, 30 transactions, 35 transactions, and ultimately 39 disputed transactions identified through reconciliation efforts. Because the underlying disputed transaction records changed depending on the representative, department, or system being reviewed, I became concerned regarding the reliability of the data used to support the investigative conclusions. Additionally, Wells Fargo 's written denial specifically stated : " The shipping address provided to the merchant for the disputed transaction ( s ) matches your address on file. '' When I challenged that statement, I explained that the address maintained on file with Wells Fargo was my mother 's residence and that I do not routinely receive packages or merchandise shipments at that address and have not done so for years. Following that challenge, the explanation provided by Wells Fargo changed from shipping address matching to billing address matching. These are materially different facts. A shipping address concerns where merchandise is delivered. A billing address concerns payment verification. As a result, I am unable to determine which factual basis was actually relied upon during the investigation. I also received an executive-level review following my original CFPB complaint. During those discussions, I was advised that the claim had been denied. However, after being informed of the denial, I was then asked multiple additional investigative questions regarding possession of the card, possession of the PIN, access to the account, and related issues. This created additional confusion because it is unclear why substantive investigative questions were still being asked if the determination had already been finalized. Conversely, if the investigation remained ongoing, it is unclear how the matter could already be considered closed. Another concern involves the investigative factors relied upon to support denial. Wells Fargo repeatedly referenced factors including : Continued possession of the physical card ; Continued possession of the PIN ; Geographic similarity ; Merchant similarity ; Digital-card activity ; and Android-device activity. However, the matter also involved a documented impersonation event in which an individual posing as a Wells Fargo representative possessed substantial account-specific information, including personal identifying information and card-related information. During that impersonation event, I was advised that an alleged unauthorized user had been added to the account and was associated with a telephone number utilizing the same XXXX area code as my own number. This raises concerns regarding the degree of weight placed upon geographic-pattern analysis and other account-association indicators when evaluating sophisticated account-compromise scenarios. Additionally, Wells Fargo has repeatedly referenced digital-card and Android-device activity as a basis supporting denial. However, I have not been provided documentation explaining how Wells Fargo determined that the device involved belonged to me rather than an unauthorized actor possessing compromised account information. My concern is that several factors cited in support of denial appear to demonstrate association with an account rather than authorization by the account holder. I am requesting review of Wells Fargo 's investigative and complaint-handling process, including : inconsistent transaction records; changing factual explanations ; conflicting shipping-address and billing-address rationales ; post-denial investigative activity ; the factual basis supporting device attribution conclusions ; and whether the investigative methodology utilized was sufficiently reliable and internally consistent under the circumstances presented. Requested Resolution : I request an independent review of Wells Fargo 's investigative process, the factual basis relied upon in support of denial, and the consistency of the records and explanations provided throughout the handling of this matter. I also request that Wells Fargo be required to clearly identify the specific evidence relied upon to support its conclusions and address the inconsistencies outlined above.

Consumer complaint narrative: On Friday, XX/XX/year>, I deposited a personal check for {$22000.00} from a client into my business checking account at Chase. I received no written notice of this exception hold from Chase. No secure message, no email, no text, no mailed notice. The only disclosure on the original deposit slip was generic boilerplate stating that further review may result in additional delay, which does not constitute the specific notice required under 12 CFR 229.13 ( g ) when a bank invokes an exception hold. The regulation requires written notice stating the specific reason for the hold and the revised availability date. I received none. I only learned about the hold by logging into the Chase app on XX/XX/XXXX, where the transaction page displayed the hold with the following stated reason : " We have not yet collected the money from the paying bank so some or all of your deposit may not be available for withdrawal. '' This stated reason was false at the time it was displayed. I have obtained confirmation from my client that the check cleared the paying bank on Monday, XX/XX/year> the same day Chase placed the exception hold citing inability to collect from the paying bank. The funds had already been debited from the issuing account on the date Chase was representing in writing that collection had not yet occurred. On XX/XX/XXXX and XX/XX/year>, I spent approximately two hours on multiple phone calls with Chase attempting to understand why availability had been extended. I received conflicting explanations from different representatives, none of which matched the stated reason displayed in the app. One representative stated Chase was unable to verify funds with the issuing bank. Another stated there was a high risk of the check being returned. The in-app reason stated funds had not yet been collected. These are three different explanations across three sources, none of which were accompanied by the written notice the regulation requires, and at least one of which ( the " not yet collected '' reason in the app ) was factually false on the date displayed. Multiple representatives told me there was nothing that could be done on the phone and that I would have to wait until XX/XX/XXXX for funds to release. After multiple escalations on XX/XX/XXXX, a supervisor released the hold during a phone call. This is itself a contradiction of what I had been told repeatedly by prior representatives that nothing could be done on the phone and the hold would not release until XX/XX/XXXX. The supervisor claimed that Chase had previously communicated the hold to me, but was unable to specify when or how that communication occurred. No such communication exists in my Chase secure messages, email, or text. The supervisor also stated that this type of hold could occur again on future deposits. The contradictions here are the core of my complaint. Either the hold was legitimate and required for the full period through XX/XX/XXXX in which case it should not have been released arbitrarily on XX/XX/XXXX after escalation or the hold was not legitimate, in which case it should not have been placed, and certainly not without the written notice the regulation requires. Both can not be true. Further, Chase 's own stated reason for the hold in the app ( " we have not yet collected the money from the paying bank '' ) was contradicted by the actual status of the check on the date the hold was placed. The funds had cleared the paying bank on XX/XX/XXXX, the same day Chase claimed in writing that collection had not occurred. Harm : Chase 's silent exception hold caused me to plan around an availability date Chase later moved without notice. I have {$14000.00} in credit card payments due XX/XX/year>, and additional auto-pays scheduled to debit this account in the coming days. Had the hold not been placed, or had it been released on its original date of XX/XX/XXXX as scheduled, these obligations would have been paid in full from the deposited funds. Because of Chase 's actions, I was preparing to incur credit card interest charges and risk of overdraft fees on auto-pays. I also lost approximately two hours of business operating time pursuing resolution by phone, during which I received contradictory and inaccurate information from multiple Chase representatives including a written representation in the Chase app that the paying bank had not collected funds, when in fact the check had cleared the paying bank on the same day the hold was placed.

During my conversation with the bank, I learned that unauthorized changes had been made to my account information. Specifically, the phone number associated with my account had been changed without my knowledge or authorization. This discovery confirmed my suspicion that an unauthorized individual had gained access to my account. The fact that my phone number had been altered is particularly important because it appears that the individual who gained access to my account used this change to bypass security measures and gain control over account communications. By changing the phone number, the individual prevented me from receiving important security notifications and may have enabled themselves to receive authentication codes intended to protect my account. During my call with PNC Bank on XX/XX/XXXX, I informed the representative that I had not authorized any of the transactions in question and that I believed my account had been compromised. The bank initiated a fraud claim and dispute regarding the unauthorized transactions. I acted immediately upon discovering the issue and did everything within my power to notify the bank and protect my account. In addition to contacting the bank, I also contacted local law enforcement on the same day. A police report was taken documenting the incident. My goal was to ensure that the matter was formally investigated and that there would be an official record showing that I reported the fraud immediately upon discovering it. I understood the seriousness of the situation and wanted to cooperate fully with both the bank and law enforcement authorities. After the initial report, I waited for the banks investigation to be completed. Several weeks later, I contacted PNC Bank to obtain an update regarding the status of my claim. At that time, I was informed that the claim had been denied. According to the explanation provided to me, the bank concluded that the transactions were not eligible for reimbursement because they involved XXXX transfers and because the transactions were allegedly authorized. I strongly disagree with that conclusion. I did not authorize these transactions. I did not initiate the transfers. I did not approve any changes to my account information. Most importantly, I reported the incident immediately after discovering it. The fact that a third-party payment platform such as XXXX was used does not change the fact that the underlying account access was unauthorized. After receiving notice of the denial, I contacted law enforcement again to follow up on the status of the investigation. During that conversation, I learned that a new detective had been assigned to the case. The detective informed me that little or no meaningful investigation had been conducted previously and that additional investigative steps would now be necessary. As a result, I was advised that the investigation would continue and that further time would be required before any conclusions could be reached. More recently, I received a letter from PNC Bank explaining the basis for the denial of my claim. The letter indicated that the bank relied on what it described as a historical pattern of use in determining that the transactions were authorized. I was extremely concerned and frustrated by this explanation because it does not address the key facts surrounding the account takeover. The critical issue is not whether I have used my account or XXXX in the past. The critical issue is that unauthorized access occurred, my phone number was changed without my permission, authentication codes were generated that I did not request, and fraudulent transactions were conducted while I was actively attempting to stop the unauthorized activity. These facts strongly suggest that my account security was compromised by someone other than myself. I subsequently contacted both PNC Bank and XXXX seeking additional information and assistance. Unfortunately, each organization directed me back to the other. XXXX advised that PNC Bank possesses the investigative information and account records. PNC Bank, meanwhile, emphasized that XXXX is a third-party service. As a result, I have been left without meaningful answers regarding who accessed my account, how the unauthorized changes occurred, where the funds were sent, and why my claim was denied despite the evidence that an account takeover occurred. I respectfully request a complete review of this matter. Specifically, I request that all records related to the investigation be reexamined, including account access logs, IP addresses, device information, phone number change records, authentication records, transaction details, and any evidence relied upon to conclude that the transactions were authorized. I also request that the bank consider the fact that I reported the fraud immediately, filed a police report, cooperated fully with all requests, and consistently maintained that I did not authorize these transactions. My objective is simple : to determine where my money went, identify the individual responsible for accessing my account, and recover the funds that were taken without my authorization. I believe the facts support my position that this was an unauthorized account takeover and not a transaction that I knowingly or willingly approved.

I am submitting this complaint regarding a pending account closure scheduled by WesBanco. This closure decision was represented as being based entirely on a specific internal allegation regarding conduct attributed to me. During the relevant period, I maintain residences in multiple locations and was residing abroad for an extended period consistent with that arrangement. I returned to Maryland on XX/XX/XXXX. During this period, I was not in a position to directly manage or immediately respond to banking communications or operational issues in real time. Separately, during this same period, I experienced significant and unresolved issues with account access and transaction processing. These issues materially disrupted normal business banking operations, including my ability to reliably monitor, access, and manage funds and transactions in support of ongoing business obligations. This occured between approximately XX/XX/XXXX until XX/XX/XXXX, when I returned. I was out of the country before the service interruption. The alleged statement forming the basis of the closure is disputed in its entirety. The communication in question occurred with my spouse present in the vehicle, and the call was conducted on speaker for its duration. I do not believe the allegation reflects an accurate or reliable characterization of what occurred, and I am not aware of any objective documentation supporting the interpretation that has been attributed to me. Based on the information available to me, I understand the institutions decision to initiate closure to be based solely on this disputed allegation rather than on documented account behavior, transactional history, or objective financial risk indicators. There has been no clear presentation of account-based evidence demonstrating that normal banking activity or risk-based criteria support this adverse action. This pending closure and the underlying circumstances are causing and will continue to cause significant and potentially irreparable harm to my business operations, financial continuity, and professional reputation, given the reliance of ongoing business activities on uninterrupted access to banking services and the downstream impact of adverse banking determinations on third-party relationships. This complaint requests supervisory review limited to whether the pending closure is supported by verified and documented account activity, whether appropriate evidentiary standards were applied prior to initiating closure of an active business account, whether account access and transaction handling during the relevant period were properly managed and documented, and whether any internal determinations relied upon are substantiated by objective facts tied to account behavior rather than unverified assertions. Additionally, review is requested to determine whether the adverse action process reflects fair, consistent, and properly documented banking practices consistent with applicable regulatory expectations for business account relationships. The requested outcome is a written explanation of the factual and documented basis for the closure decision, identification of the specific account activity relied upon for the adverse action, a full review of account access and transaction handling during the relevant period, correction of any unsupported internal determinations if identified, and confirmation that any closure action is grounded in verified facts and consistent with fair banking standards.

Consumer complaint narrative: On XXXX XXXX XXXX, my XXXX debit card was used to pay a {$170.00} charge at XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in XXXX, Tennessee. The hotel processed a refund of {$170.00} back to the same card on XX/XX/XXXX, at XXXX XXXX confirmed by the hotel 's folio and by the XXXX merchant transaction record ( both already provided to the bank ). The refund never appeared in my account. On or about XX/XX/XXXX, I called the bank by phone to notify it of this disputed transaction. My authorized representative also called the bank the same day, separately, on my behalf. The representatives on both calls handled by two different bank reps on the same day advised us NOT to file a formal dispute, stating that doing so would " make it take longer '' or " elongate the refund. '' This consistent advice, delivered to two separate callers by two different representatives on the same day, steered me away from formally invoking my Regulation E rights at the moment notice was actually given. The fact that the same advice was given by separate representatives on the same day suggests this was not an isolated rep error but a practice or scripted response. Under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( b ) ( 1 ), oral notice of a Reg E error triggers the bank 's investigation obligation. The bank may require written follow-up only if it informs the consumer of that requirement at the time of the oral notice which is the opposite of what the bank 's representatives did on XX/XX/XXXX. The 10-business-day window from the XX/XX/XXXX oral notice has now elapsed, and the bank has issued no provisional credit. The bank has subsequently stated, in email correspondence, that the dispute could take " 60120 days '' because the bank was " waiting on the merchant to respond. '' This response conflates two separate processes : the XXXX chargeback / back-end merchant settlement process ( which can run 60120 days ) and the consumer 's rights under Regulation E ( which require the bank to either complete its investigation within 10 business days or provisionally credit the disputed amount under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ). The 60120 day chargeback timeline is not a permissible basis to withhold provisional credit on the front end. The documentation already provided to the bank shows that the merchant issued the refund on XX/XX/XXXX, with an authorization number, token, and invoice number. The dispute is not about whether the merchant will refund the merchant has refunded. The question is where that refund went between the merchant 's processor and my account, which is precisely the type of error Regulation E provisional credit is designed to address during investigation. I am filing this complaint regarding three concerns : 1. The bank 's discouragement of a formal dispute filing on XX/XX/XXXX advice given consistently to two separate callers on the same day by different representatives. This pattern steered me away from exercising my Regulation E rights and may constitute a deceptive practice under UDAAP. I am specifically requesting that the Bureau ask the bank whether the " don't file/ it will take longer '' advice was a scripted, trained, or otherwise institutional response, as the consistency of the advice across two different reps on the same day suggests it was not an individual error. 2. The bank 's conflation of merchant chargeback timelines with Regulation E provisional credit obligations, which is being used as a stated reason to withhold provisional credit my account is entitled to under 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( c ). 3. The bank 's failure to follow Regulation E error-resolution procedures, including the failure to disclose my right to a formal dispute at the time of the XX/XX/XXXX oral notice. Relief requested : ( a ) immediate provisional credit of {$170.00} to my account pending completion of the investigation, as required by 12 C.F.R. 1005.11 ( c ) ; ( b ) a written explanation of the bank 's Regulation E procedures and whether the XX/XX/XXXX " don't file '' advice reflects scripted or trained representative responses ; and ( c ) any further corrective action the Bureau deems appropriate. Documents available and previously provided to the bank : the hotel folio dated XX/XX/XXXX ; the XXXX XXXX Transaction Manager record confirming the XX/XX/XXXX refund authorization ; email correspondence with the bank 's representative.

CFPB, I am submitting this complaint regarding JPMorgan Chase Banks handling of a recent check deposit and the repeated, inconsistent information I have received from its representatives concerning the availability of my funds. On XXXX, I deposited a check into my Chase account. After making the deposit, I contacted Chase on multiple occasions to inquire about the status of the deposit and when the funds would become available. Relying on the information provided by Chase representatives, I expected the funds to become available in accordance with the timeframe that had been communicated to me. However, after receiving the same information from multiple representatives, I was later provided with conflicting information by another representative, who indicated that the funds would not be available until a later date. As a consumer, I depend on the accuracy of information provided by my financial institution. When I contact a bank regarding the availability of deposited funds, I reasonably expect that the information I receive will be accurate, consistent, and based on the actual status of my account. Instead, I was provided with conflicting explanations regarding the same transaction. This has left me uncertain as to which information is correct and has undermined my confidence in the information being provided by Chase. My concern extends beyond the timing of this particular deposit. My primary concern is the apparent inconsistency in the information communicated by Chase representatives. If a deposit is subject to a hold, review, or delayed availability, customers should be provided with a clear and consistent explanation. If no hold exists, customers should likewise receive consistent information regarding when funds will become available. Receiving multiple different answers from the same institution regarding the same transaction is unacceptable and creates unnecessary confusion. Additionally, the conflicting information caused me to spend significant time contacting Chase in an effort to obtain a clear answer. Rather than receiving a definitive explanation, I was forced to continue seeking clarification because the information provided by one representative contradicted the information provided by another. Consumers should not have to navigate inconsistent explanations from their bank in order to determine when they will have access to their own funds. I am concerned that there may be deficiencies in employee training, internal communication, account documentation, or customer service procedures that contributed to this situation. If representatives are reviewing the same account information yet providing different answers, that raises legitimate concerns regarding the reliability of the information being provided to customers. I respectfully request that JPMorgan Chase conduct a thorough review of this matter, including a review of account notes, deposit records, call logs, and any recordings of my communications with the bank. I would like Chase to determine why I received conflicting information regarding the availability of my deposit and whether the information provided to me was accurate.

I am submitting this complaint regarding Bank of America 's handling of my business checking account. Concerned by this activity, I contacted Bank of America and was informed that the account was frozen. I subsequently spoke with Client Recoveries and was advised that the account appeared to be in the process of closing. I was instructed to wait 24 to 48 hours for the system to update. After waiting, I contacted the bank again on XX/XX/XXXX and was informed that the account status had returned to open and active. On XX/XX/XXXX, the deposited funds became available as promised, and I began using my debit card and account normally. However, on Saturday, XX/XX/XXXX, I attempted to use an ATM and was informed that no transactions could be processed on the account. I immediately visited a Bank of America branch and spoke with the branch manager. The branch manager advised that the account had been frozen again. She stated there were no alerts, notes, or explanations visible on the account indicating why the freeze had been placed. She further advised that the account appeared to be frozen rather than closed and provided me with the telephone number for Client Protection. I then contacted customer service and spoke with a representative named XXXX. XXXX advised that there were no notes or alerts explaining the situation. He could see that I had been actively using the account and stated that the issue appeared to be an internal Bank of America matter. He further stated that it appeared a simple code correction changing the account status from frozen to open would resolve the issue. XXXX directed me to contact Client Recoveries when they reopened. On Monday, I spent approximately nine hours, from XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX., attempting to obtain answers regarding why my account had been refrozen. During these calls, I spoke with multiple representatives and supervisors, including Supervisor XXXX XXXX. I was advised that Client Recoveries was not the correct department and that Deposit Services would instead handle the issue. When transferred to Deposit Services, representatives were unable to explain why the account had been refrozen and, contrary to what Client Recoveries had previously stated, informed me that the account was actually closed. This directly contradicted information I had received from both Client Recoveries and branch personnel, who had repeatedly advised that the account was frozen, not closed. I was then referred back to Client Recoveries, where representative XXXX advised me once again to wait 24 to 48 hours and " see what happens. '' When I asked why I had never received any notice that my account would be frozen, he stated that customers would not receive notice unless the account was formally closed. On XX/XX/XXXX, I spoke with another Client Recoveries representative, I. XXXX, who stated that their department could not take any action unless the account was closed and attempted to transfer me yet again to another department. At this point, Client Protection, Client Recoveries, Deposit Services, customer service representatives, supervisors, and branch personnel have all provided conflicting information. No one has been able to explain : Why the account was initially frozen. Why a forced closure transaction appeared and was then reversed. Why the account was returned to open and active status on XX/XX/XXXX. Why the account was frozen again after funds became available and I resumed normal account activity. Whether the account is frozen or closed. Why no alerts, notes, or documentation exist explaining the status of the account. Why I was never provided notice regarding the freeze. As a business owner, I have deposits that need to be made into this account and ongoing business transactions that can not be completed because Bank of America has restricted access to the account without explanation. The bank 's inability to provide accurate information, identify the responsible department, or explain its actions has caused significant disruption to my business operations. I am requesting that Bank of America provide a complete written explanation regarding the status of my account, identify the reason for the freezes and any closure actions, restore access if the account remains open, and explain why no notice was provided. I also request that the CFPB require Bank of America to investigate the conflicting information provided by its various departments and provide a definitive resolution. If Bank of America is unable or unwilling to provide answers regarding this matter, I intend to pursue additional remedies through the Illinois Attorney General 's Office and any other appropriate regulatory agencies.
